title.narrative: PSI Ensuring SRHR For All in Zimbabwe 2022-25
PSI Säkerställa tillgång till SRHR för alla i Zimbabwe 2022-25

description.narrative: Objectives -Communications and mobilization efforts remove barriers to accessing SRHR services -A bringing care closer service delivery approach increases access for marginalized populations -Total market development approach for condoms, Emergency Contraceptive and Menstrual Health removes systemic barriers to sustainable market solutions -Quality of care systems for SRHR services are improved to provide enhanced client-centered care Anticipated Outcomes -Unintended pregnancies averted Users reached with SRHR products and services -Couple Years of Protection generated from Family Planning products and service providers capacity strengthened to deliver friendly and comprehensive SRHR services -Increased agency and self-efficacy of users to demand responsive SRHR services -Increased knowledge and uptake of SGBV services within 72 hours The contribution aims to provide cervical cancer prevention services 40,000 women, deliver 280,000 couple years of protection through modern contraceptives, treat 7,500 people for STIs, and provide services for 4,000 survivors of sexual violence, reaching a total of 240,000 users of SRH services.

Population Services International (PSI) tillsammans med sina partners - Population Solutions for Health (PSH), Adult Rape Clinic (ARC) och Family Support Trust (FST), Rights (SRHR) lämnade in ett uppföljningsprogramförslag för en fas II av "Säkerställa tillgång till sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR) för alla i Zimbabwe" för en andra fas (fas II) av "Säkerställa tillgång till sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR) för alla i Zimbabwe". Fas II-visionen är att föra vården närmare utsatta konsumenter som programmet syftar till att tjäna, öka byrån, valet och rösten för marginaliserade befolkningar som är minst benägna att söka tjänster i traditionella miljöer, inklusive utsatta tonårsflickor och unga kvinnor, fattiga kvinnor i städer och på landsbygden i reproduktiv ålder, medlemmar av nyckelpopulationer och personer med funktionsnedsättning.
Programmet syftar till att öka tillgången till ett komplett utbud av tjänster för sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa i ett rättighetsbaserat tillvägagångssätt som syftar till att avlägsna individuella, familje-, samhälls- och samhällshinder för tillgång, för att minska oavsiktliga graviditeter, förebygga och behandla sexuellt överförbara infektioner, förbättra menstruationshälsan och hygienen som en ingång till SRHR-paketet, tillhandahålla och främja leverans och stöd efter våldtäkt, och förebygga livmoderhalscancer.
Projektet kommer att lägga ett särskilt fokus på att nå dem som är kvar, inklusive ungdomar, överlevande av sexuellt våld, migranter, PLWD, PLHIV, de fattigaste av de fattiga, de som bor i avlägsna områden och andra marginaliserade grupper. Insatsen syftar till att tillhandahålla 40 000 kvinnor för förebyggande av livmoderhalscancer, leverera 280 000 par års skydd genom moderna preventivmedel, behandla 7 500 personer för STI och tillhandahålla tjänster för 4 000 överlevande av sexuellt våld och nå totalt 240 000 användare av SRH-tjänster.
För att uppnå sina mål kommer Population Services International (PSI) kommer att ha implementeringsavtal med lokala partners Population Solutions for Health, Adult Rape Clinic (ARC) och Family Support Trust (FST). PSI kommer att ha ett övergripande ansvar över sina partners och kommer att ansvara för att uppnå mål och rapportering.

Population Services International (PSI) together with its partners – Population Solutions for Health (PSH), Adult Rape Clinic (ARC) and Family Support Trust (FST), Rights (SRHR) submitted a follow on programme proposal for a Phase II of the “Ensuring Access to Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) for All in Zimbabwe”for a second phase (Phase II) of “Ensuring Access to Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) for All in Zimbabwe”. The Phase II vision is to bring care closer to vulnerable consumers the program seeks to serve, increasing agency, choice and voice for marginalized populations who are least likely to seek services in traditional settings, including vulnerable adolescent girls and young women, urban and rural poor women of reproductive age, members of key populations communities, and people with disabilities. The program seeks to increase access to a full range of sexual and reproductive health services in a rights-based approach which seeks to remove individual, family, community, and societal barriers to access, to reduce unintended pregnancies, prevent and treat sexually transmitted infections, improve menstrual health and hygiene as an entry point to the SRHR package, provide and promote post-rape service delivery and support, and prevent cervical cancer.
The project will place a particular focus on reaching those left behind, including youth, survivors of sexual violence, migrants, PLWD, PLHIV, the poorest of the poor, those living in remote areas, and other marginalized groups. The contribution aims to provide cervical cancer prevention services 40,000 women, deliver 280,000 couple years of protection through modern contraceptives, treat 7,500 people for STIs, and provide services for 4,000 survivors of sexual violence, reaching a total of 240,000 users of SRH services.
To achieve its objectives, Population Services International (PSI) will have implementation agreements with local partners Population Solutions for Health, Adult Rape Clinic (ARC) and Family Support Trust (FST). PSI will have an overall responsibility over its partners and will be responsible for delivery of objectives and reporting.

2023 RESULTS Year 2 of the programme implementation was characterised by easing of Covid restrictions which improved the operational environment and access to services by the beneficiaries. Staff attrition remains a challenge in the public sector and PSH continues its efforts to address the gaps by training additional service providers and providing technical support.
The economy continued to be unstable in the period under review threatening access to service as people had little out of pocket to cater for their health and the majority of clients (70%) were reached through this channel. PSI reported that a total of 171,162 Couple Years of Protection (CYPs) were delivered by the end of Phase II year 2, bringing the life of the project total CYPs to 336,941, a 96% achievement to the projected 350,000 CYPs. Condoms and implants remained the top contraception of choice.
•71,016 unintended pregnancies averted
•13,444 unsafe abortions averted
•94% of eligible women of those screened for cervical cancer received preventive treatment
•51% of clients were <25yrs old
•20% of clients received Long-acting reversible contraceptives
•The programme introduced aetiological diagnosis of chlamydia and gonorrhoea
•67% of STI clients were <25yrs old, and mostly female
Ninety one percent of gender-based violence survivors are women and minors. Survivors of gender-based violence continue to present late for clinical check-ups ( Only 23% reported within 72hrs) which calls for intensive and innovative awareness campaigns.
The static sites also reached the poorest with 48% of the clients receiving program services at New Start clinics being categorised as living in extreme poverty, based on the World Banks poverty lines methodology used to measure socio-economic status. Sixty four percent of those receiving contraception were adolescent girls and young women and 54% of the AGYWs received oral contraceptives which remains the method of choice for adolescent girls and young women.
Partner is intentionally making efforts to reach the vulnerable women with diabilities through outreach services partnering with national disability organisations.
2022 RESULTS -The programme reached 295,730 recipients of care with SRH services across 27 districts and distributed 7,518,920 pieces of male condoms in all districts of the country through social marketing and free offer to key populations.
-To support uptake of SRHR products and services, radio shows, social media, google ads and interpersonal communications platforms reached up to 3.1M individuals.
- Subcutaneously Administered Depot Medroxyprogesterone Acetate (DMPA-SC) self-injection was employed in all New Start service delivery location, resulting in efficient service delivery through expanded choice for self-care technologies. Study findings from the DMPA-SC operations research were presented at the International Conference on Family Planning (ICFP) in November 2022.
-Self-collection of Human Papilloma Virus DNA samples was done at all sites. The program published a success story on the PSH website (psh.org.zw) titled bringing Care into the hands of the Users: Closing Cervical Cancer Screening Coverage Gap Through HPV DNA Self-Sample Collection.
PSI submitted a revised results framework with more realistic targets following the over achievements in the first year of reporting.
